level1.text: The attenuation coefficient of a telecommunications fibre is $0.18\,\text{dB/km}$. What is the attenuation of a fibre $50\,\text{km}$ long, in decibels?
The power of light is $2.0\,\text{mW}$ at the start of a fibre and $0.50\,\text{mW}$ at the end. What is the attenuation of the fibre in decibels?

Assume that the eddy currents in the base of a pan on an induction hob can be described as one current loop with a resistance of $0.010\,\Omega$, in which flows an alternating current with an effective value of $400\,\text{A}$. At what power do the eddy currents change electrical energy into internal energy of the base? Give the answer in kilowatts.

The magnetic field of a wireless charger is uniform at the receiver coil of a phone and perpendicular to the plane of the coil, and the peak value of the magnetic flux density is $0.50\,\text{mT}$. The area of one turn of the coil is $12\,\text{cm}^2$. What is the peak value of the flux through one turn? Give the answer in microwebers.

Assume that a wireless charger takes a power of $10.0\,\text{W}$ from the wall socket and a power of $7.2\,\text{W}$ is transferred to the battery of the phone. What is the efficiency of the charging? Give the answer as a percentage.

level2.text: The receiver coil of a phone has $10$ turns. The frequency of the charger is $140\,\text{kHz}$, and the magnetic flux through one turn varies sinusoidally with a peak value of $0.40\,\mu\text{Wb}$. What is the peak value of the voltage induced in the coil?

The transmitter of a fibre link feeds a power of $1.0\,\text{mW}$ into the fibre, and the receiver detects the pulses when the power is at least $1.0\,\mu\text{W}$. The attenuation coefficient of the fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$. What is the greatest possible length of the link without an amplifier? Ignore the attenuation of the splices.

The cooking zone of an induction hob takes a power of $2.0\,\text{kW}$ from the mains. Assume that $85\,\%$ of the power is transferred to the water in the pan. The pan contains $1.5\,\text{kg}$ of water at a temperature of $15\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How long does it take to heat the water to the boiling point, $100\,{}^\circ\text{C}$? The specific heat capacity of water is $4190\,\tfrac{\text{J}}{\text{kg}\cdot\text{K}}$. Give the answer in minutes.

In a measurement (Ravenscraft, OneZero, 2020) charging a phone from empty to full took $14.26\,\text{Wh}$ of energy from the wall socket with a cable charger and $21.01\,\text{Wh}$ with a charging pad. Assume that the phone is charged from empty to full once a day for a year ($365$ days). How much more energy does the charging pad use in a year than the cable charger? Give the answer in kilowatt-hours.

level3.text:
The submarine cable C-Lion1 is $1172\,\text{km}$ long (Cinia, 2016).

Assume that the attenuation coefficient of its fibres is $0.18\,\text{dB/km}$ and that the attenuation of one section of fibre may be at most $20\,\text{dB}$ before an optical amplifier restores the power of the light. The sections are of equal length, and the amplifiers are between the sections; the transmitter and the receiver are at the ends of the cable.

What is the smallest number of amplifiers the cable must have?

The coil of an induction hob at a frequency of $25\,\text{kHz}$ produces in the base of a pan a sinusoidally varying magnetic field whose magnetic flux density has a peak value of $4.0\,\text{mT}$.

Assume that the field is uniform and perpendicular to the base, that the eddy currents in the base can be described as one loop with a radius of $8.0\,\text{cm}$ and a resistance of $0.050\,\Omega$, and that the magnetic field of the eddy current itself is ignored.

At what mean power does the base heat up? Give the answer in kilowatts.

The transmitter of a fibre link feeds a power of $1.0\,\text{mW}$ into the fibre, and the receiver needs a power of at least $10\,\mu\text{W}$. The attenuation coefficient of the fibre is $0.20\,\text{dB/km}$, and the link has four splices, each of which attenuates by $0.50\,\text{dB}$.

The refractive index of the glass of the fibre is $1.47$.

How long does it take a light pulse to travel from end to end of the longest possible link, when the pulse travels along the axis of the fibre? The speed of light in a vacuum is $3.00 \cdot 10^8\,\text{m/s}$. Give the answer in milliseconds.
